draft.title: Biomass productivity
card: Biomass productivity is how much plant matter a biome grows each year. Plants are the base of the food supply for animals in that biome.
Plants need light, warmth and water to grow. Where all three are plentiful, plants grow fast and in large amounts.
Warm, wet places such as tropical rainforests and wetlands grow the most plant matter each year.
Cold or dry biomes grow the least. Tundra is too cold for much of the year, and deserts have very little water.
draft.remember: Plants grow most where it is warm and wet, and least where it is cold or dry.

a.q: Which of these places grows the most plant matter in a year?
a.why: A tropical rainforest is warm and wet all year, so plants grow fast. Tundra is the most tempting wrong option, but it is too cold for much of the year, so its biomass productivity is low.
a.clue: Think of the biome with both warmth and water.

b.q: Two regions get similar sunshine. Region X has a wetland with water all year. Region Y is dry with little rain. Which statement about their biomass productivity is best?
opts: X is higher because it has more water
Y is higher because dry air gives more light
They match because they get similar sunshine
Y is higher because plants there grow slowly
b.why: With similar sunshine, water decides the difference. Region X has plenty of water, so its plants grow more each year. Matching sunshine does not make them equal, because plants need water as well as light.
b.clue: Light is equal, so look at what differs.

b.best: X is higher because it has more water
